name: User activation and idle inference
plain: Tells whether the person has clicked or typed recently, and in Chromium whether they are idle.
meaning: navigator.userActivation shows if a click or key happened. IdleDetector (permission gated, Chromium) reports user active or idle and screen locked. Without it, sites infer idle from the absence of input events.

firefox.note: BCD lists no support; agent research says otherwise

safari.note: BCD lists no support; agent research says otherwise

ios_safari.note: BCD lists no support; agent research says otherwise

data.metric: userState: active or idle, screenState: locked or unlocked

limits.headline: Can see if you recently clicked or typed, and in Chromium if you are idle
limits.user_action: You click or type on the page. Idle checks need you to tap Allow
can: Tell if you clicked or pressed a key lately
In Chromium, learn if you are active or idle, after you allow it
In Chromium, learn if your screen is locked, after you allow it
cannot: See what you typed or clicked, only that you did
Get idle checks in Firefox or Safari
Get idle checks without your Allow
Learn why you are idle or what you are doing
limits.differs: The idle permission works in Chrome and Edge only. The simple click check works in every browser.

story.what_it_is: A page can tell if you recently clicked or typed, and in Chromium, with permission, whether you are idle.

marketing.name: Idle Detection API
marketing.pitch: Chrome says it lets apps like chat know when you are away from the device, with your permission.

marketing.name: User activation
marketing.pitch: Explains that some features only work right after a real click or key press.

story.for_you: Some features, like opening a popup, only work right after you tap or click. For the idle check, Chromium asks first, then a chat app can mark you as away or active.
story.for_makers: User activation stops pages from playing sound or opening windows without you. Idle detection helps chat and collaboration apps show real presence and send notifications to the right device.

use_cases.example: A work chat web app marks you away after you leave the computer, then sends alerts to your phone.
A shared document editor shows who is active right now so teammates know who is working.
A browser game only starts sound and video after your first click, because browsers require it.
A video site pauses or lowers quality when you step away, to save data.
A banking site logs you out when you are idle, after a few minutes without activity.
An ad site only counts a video as viewed if you interacted, which stops bots that play videos.
An online exam page notes long idle gaps to review for possible cheating.

technical_bounds: IdleDetector is Chromium only, 60 s minimum threshold, requires permission
Never shows which apps are active
